solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

R047-01.notes: Passage builds to 'the beetles were steering not by particular stars but by the glow of the Milky Way as a whole' and closes with 'the researchers were careful about what it did not show.' B contradicted ('not navigating to a destination'; not particular stars); C wrong reason (thieves, not energy); D unsupported overgeneralization.

R047-02.notes: P1: 'other beetles at the same pile would rather steal a finished ball... The safest strategy is to leave quickly, and the fastest way to leave a crowded spot is to travel in a straight line.' A, C, D unsupported; D inverts the point (returning means 'among the thieves').

R047-03.notes: P3 reports the moon/polarized-light finding, then 'That finding raised a further question... What were they steering by?' A = P2 content; B unsupported (no misunderstanding claimed); C = P4/P5 content.

flags: minor: key is the longest choice
R047-04.notes: P4: 'beetles fitted with small cardboard visors that blocked their view of the sky... wandered, while beetles fitted with transparent visors did not.' Transparent visors are a control for the visor itself. A unsupported (no 'clearer view'); B wrong (test was outdoors); D not the purpose (individual stars not at issue in this test).

R047-05.notes: P4: 'When it showed only a diffuse band of light corresponding to the Milky Way, with no individual stars, they still kept a steady course.' A includes stars so doesn't isolate; C and D show sky is needed, not that individual stars are unnecessary.

flags: minor: overlaps conceptually with R047-05 (both turn on individual stars not being needed) but neither reveals the other's key
R047-06.notes: P5: 'a beetle's compound eyes are probably not sharp enough to pick out most individual stars, while the bright band of the galaxy is visible to them.' C contradicted ('does not need to know where it is going'); A, B unsupported.

R047-07.notes: P6: 'The beetles were not navigating to a destination, as migrating birds do; they were simply holding a straight line.' B, C, D unsupported.

R047-08.notes: 'to fix its bearings on something in the sky' = establish/set its orientation. Repair is the common-meaning trap; arrange and attach do not fit 'bearings'.

flags: minor: key is the longest choice and the only one that echoes a specific cue ('the moon when it is up') from the final sentence
R047-09.notes: P6: 'the experiments did not rule out the possibility that, under some skies, the beetles also use other cues, such as the brightest stars or the moon when it is up.' A contradicts the starry-sky/outdoor results; B contradicts 'not navigating to a destination'; C contradicts the outdoor visor test.

R047-10.notes: P2: 'The beetle pushes the ball backward with its hind legs while walking on its front legs, head down, facing away from where it is going.' D distorts the pre-departure 'dance' ('Before setting off'); B, C contradicted. Near-verbatim lift; very easy.

R047-11.notes: P1: described as 'a sign business' 'in the tone people use for a relative who has taken up the accordion' -- mild condescension toward an eccentric, unserious pursuit. A opposite tone; C over-literal (she names it accurately); D unsupported.

R047-12.notes: P3: 'when an owner wanted the gold leaf that the print shop could not imitate.' B, C, D are print-shop advantages ('in an afternoon,' 'four hundred typefaces,' 'for less').

R047-13.notes: 'she studied them the way other people read letters' -- treating the photos as personal, meaningful documents deserving close attention; ties to families wanting signs 'to look the way the old one had.' B overly specific ('exactly'); C misreads 'letters' literally; D contradicted ('by painters who had died before I was born').

R047-14.notes: P4: 'By the third week, my O's had stopped sagging. I was promoted to the rest of the alphabet and then, in August, to a real job: the name of a hardware store'; bus ride is 'that evening' after the job. Order C, B, A, D.

flags: minor: the passage's own simile ('like water collecting in a footprint') supplies the key word 'collected' almost verbatim, making the item very easy
R047-15.notes: 'the paint pooled at the bottom of each stroke like water collecting in a footprint.' Shared is the common-meaning trap; thinned/dried don't fit.
